summary: @myorder-frontend-commons/analytics exfiltrates host identity via install-time beacon
details: The package declares preinstall, install, and postinstall lifecycle hooks that all execute poc.js on `npm install`. poc.js collects host identification data (hostname, username, platform, architecture, OS release, cwd, Node.js version, package version, npm_lifecycle_event, and the names of CI-related environment variables) and transmits it over two channels to non-first-party collectors: an HTTP GET request to 80-190-83-27.nip.io carrying the fields in the query path, and a DNS lookup where a hex-encoded `hostname|user|pkgVersion` string is used as a subdomain label under db4jftohu4noreqdanngpnb3ger45ykrt.oast.fun so the identity leaks even when HTTP egress is blocked. The @myorder-frontend-commons scope and the install-time beacon shape are consistent with a dependency-confusion reconnaissance payload targeting internal environments that resolve this public scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
